card.text: Dusty red planet with the largest volcano in the solar system.

introduction.text: Mars is a cold desert with a very thin atmosphere. Its seasons last longer than Earth's.

normal.title: MDIM 2.1 colorized global mosaic
normal.summary: Viking images with NASA Ames color; lighting and resolution vary.

elevation.title: Height of mountains and basins
elevation.summary: Laser measurements reveal Mars’s mountains and deep basins; colors show height relative to a gravity-based zero level.

thermal.title: THEMIS daytime infrared mosaic
thermal.summary: Daytime infrared brightness from combined observations. Black bands at the edges are missing coverage.

water-equivalent.title: Odyssey GRS water equivalent
water-equivalent.summary: Hydrogen expressed as equivalent water. Source gaps and negative estimates remain visible.

chlorine.title: Odyssey GRS chlorine
chlorine.summary: Chlorine is an element often found in salts; colors estimate its amount in the upper layer of Martian ground.

iron.title: Odyssey GRS iron
iron.summary: Iron is an ingredient of many rocks; colors estimate its amount in the upper layer of Martian ground.

silicon.title: Odyssey GRS silicon
silicon.summary: Silicon occurs in most rock-forming minerals; colors estimate its amount in the upper layer of Martian ground.

potassium.title: Odyssey GRS potassium
potassium.summary: Potassium occurs in some rock-forming minerals; colors estimate its amount in the upper layer of Martian ground.

thorium.title: Odyssey GRS thorium
thorium.summary: Thorium is a naturally radioactive element in rocks; colors estimate its amount in the upper layer of Martian ground.

geology.title: USGS SIM 3292 geologic units
geology.summary: Forty-four interpreted geologic units in the published map colors.

magnetic.title: Langlais 2019 radial field
magnetic.summary: Radial crustal field inferred from MGS and MAVEN. Features smaller than about 160 km are unresolved.

crust.title: Wieczorek 2022 crust model
crust.summary: Model with 39 km beneath InSight and uniform crust density; one published example.

heat-flow-now.title: Modeled heat flow today
heat-flow-now.summary: Heat leaving Mars’s interior through the ground today, in a model; it has never been measured on the surface.

heat-flow-1-5-ga.title: Heat flow 1.5 billion years ago
heat-flow-1-5-ga.summary: The same model 1.5 billion years ago, when more of the interior’s radioactive heat remained.

heat-flow-3-0-ga.title: Heat flow 3.0 billion years ago
heat-flow-3-0-ga.summary: The same model 3.0 billion years ago: about twice today’s heat flow.

heat-flow-3-5-ga.title: Heat flow 3.5 billion years ago
heat-flow-3-5-ga.summary: The same model 3.5 billion years ago: two and a half times today’s heat flow.

albedo.title: MGS TES surface albedo
albedo.summary: How much sunlight the ground reflects. Bright areas are dusty; dark areas are sand and rock.

thermal-inertia.title: How fast the ground heats and cools
thermal-inertia.summary: Dust heats and cools quickly; sand and rock hold their temperature. Measured from nightside temperatures.

dust-cover.title: Where dust covers the ground
dust-cover.summary: An infrared index of fine dust cover: low values are dusty, high values dust-free.

dune-fields.title: USGS dune database fields
dune-fields.summary: Moderate to large dune fields mapped in THEMIS images, 65° N to 65° S. Unmarked ground may still hold sand.

valley-networks.title: Hynek global valley network map
valley-networks.summary: Ancient river valleys mapped across Mars, shown by the 5.2 km cells each valley line crosses.

alluvial-fans.title: Large alluvial fans in craters
alluvial-fans.summary: 44 large fans of water-carried sediment inside craters, each marked by the 5.2 km cell holding it.

gullies.title: CTX global gully survey
gullies.summary: Young gullies on slopes, colored by the direction they face; each 5.2 km cell holds at least one.

glacier-like-forms.title: Martian glacier-like form inventory
glacier-like-forms.summary: 1,309 small ice-rich glaciers in the mid-latitudes, each marked by the 5.2 km cell at its centre.

recessional-glfs.title: Glacier-like forms that have shrunk
recessional-glfs.summary: 436 glacier-like forms with strong evidence of retreat since a last glacial maximum, one 5.2 km cell each.

glacial-valleys.title: Valleys cut by glacial meltwater
glacial-valleys.summary: Small valleys carved by meltwater on or beside Amazonian glaciers, one 5.2 km cell each.

recent-activity.title: Changes seen by HiRISE
recent-activity.summary: New craters, active gullies and seasonal slope streaks seen forming in repeat HiRISE images.

hydrous-minerals.title: CRISM and OMEGA hydrous detections
hydrous-minerals.summary: Where infrared spectrometers detected water-altered minerals such as clays and hydrated salts.

aqueous-classes.title: Water-formed mineral classes
aqueous-classes.summary: Clays, sulfates, silica, chlorides and carbonates found from orbit, one 5.2 km cell per site.

chloride-deposits.title: THEMIS chloride-bearing deposits
chloride-deposits.summary: Salt deposits found in infrared images. Deposits under about 5 km across fall between map cells.
